Subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Hi Jessica — great to talk earlier. Thanks for walking through Acuity's product flow and the projected volumes (chat assistant + summarization). Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Recap:
- Expected steady-state usage: ~200–300M tokens/month (mix of assistant prompts + long summaries).
- Primary requirements: predictable unit economics, on-prem / VPC option for PHI, latency SLOs for live-assist flows.
- Success metrics for the pilot: cost per 1M tokens target, 99th percentile latency <250ms for 1–2k RPS bursts, and no PII leakage in logs.

Pricing/qualification questions we discussed (can you confirm):
- Target budget range for unit cost: $/1M tokens target you mentioned was $6k–$7k?
- Do you have a hard cap for monthly spend or flexibility for a committed volume/discount?

What I attached: a one-sheet benchmarking workbook comparing Redwood net unit pricing vs typical host/managed options (OpenAI/Anthropic/hosted open-model vendors) under a few compression/quantization assumptions. See tab “Assumptions & Examples”.

Next proposed steps:
1) You confirm the target $/1M tokens band and monthly volume (best estimate).
2) We run a short unit-economic POC (1–2 weeks) with representative prompts — Aditya will scope the technical setup and instrumentation.
3) If the POC looks good, we’ll scope Dedicated or Private pricing with a committed volume for discounting.

I’m looping in Aditya (solutions) and Marissa (pricing) to help with the POC scope and to put numbers behind the benchmarking. Happy to hop on a quick follow-up call early next week.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

- Yes, $6k–$7k / 1M tokens is the ballpark budget we’d like to stay within for production (after any committed discounts).

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Hi Jessica — great questions. See inline + attached ROI examples (tab “250M examples”) in the workbook. Quick highlights here so you can share with Tom: 

Unit economics assumptions we used (documented in the workbook):
- Token multiplier: 1.45x (average ratio to account for system tokens, meta instructions, and multi-turn chat).
- Effective compression via quantization / shorter context kernels: 20–30% cost reduction for compatible open models in Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Pricing is presented as $ per 1M "billable" tokens (post-multiplier).

Benchmarking numbers (reference comparisons in the attached sheet):
- Redwood (recommended target for Acuity): $6,500 / 1M tokens — this assumes a committed volume match (~250M/mo) and a Dedicated capacity profile with int8/4-bit quantization on open models.
- OpenAI (public GPT-tier equivalents): ~$10,000 / 1M tokens (typical hosted price for comparable quality endpoints).
- Anthropic (Claude-style hosted): ~$9,000–11,000 / 1M tokens depending on model and service tier.
- Other open-model hosts (varies): $5,500–$9,000 / 1M depending on their discounting, quantization support, and whether they require lift-and-shift infra fees.

Example ROI (rounded):
- At 250M billable tokens/month:
  - @ $6,500 /1M -> ~$1.625M / month
  - @ $8,000 /1M -> ~$2.0M / month
  - @ $10,000 /1M -> ~$2.5M / month

Notes and seller-side levers: 
- Committed volume discounts: we can structure stepped pricing at volume thresholds (e.g., 200M+, 400M+).
- Pilot credits: yes, we commonly provide pilot credits (covers part of POC cost) and a short-term trial rate to validate latency and quality before moving to committed pricing.
- Private deployment overhead: there’s a one-time onboarding/infra fee for a Private/VPC install; Dedicated removes most infra variability and is where the most predictable unit economics come from.

Next steps I suggest: 
- Aditya to propose a POC scope and instrumentation checklist (1–2 weeks).
- Marissa to draft a provisional pricing sheet (committed tiers + pilot credit language).
- Jessica/Tom to confirm preferred PO/contract cadence and any internal approval timelines.

I’ve attached the benchmarking workbook (redwood_vs_hosts_token_pricing.xlsx) and a short mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_acuity.pdf).

Thanks — looping Aditya and Marissa to take action.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
